questions.q:
Regarding BGP, consider the following statements.
I. BGP is a path-vector routing protocol.
II. BGP is classified as an interior gateway protocol.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only I is correct. BGP exchanges path information between autonomous systems, so it is an exterior gateway protocol. Interior protocols such as OSPF and RIP work inside one autonomous system.

questions.q: The first octet range of class D (multicast) IPv4 addresses is
questions.e: Class D addresses begin with the bits 1110, giving 224 to 239. Class E (240 to 255) is reserved.

questions.q: The network address of the host 192.168.10.77/26 is
questions.e: A /26 mask is 255.255.255.192. 77 AND 192 = 64, so the network address is 192.168.10.64.

questions.q: A 16-QAM signal is sent at 2400 baud. The bit rate is
questions.e: 16-QAM has 16 states, so each signal element carries log₂16 = 4 bits. Bit rate = 2400 × 4 = 9600 bps.

questions.q: Match the protocols in List I with their default ports in List II.
questions.e: SMTP uses 25, DNS uses 53, Telnet uses 23 and POP3 uses 110.

questions.q: A 1000-byte packet is sent on a 1 Mbps link. The transmission delay is
questions.e: Transmission delay = packet size / bandwidth = 8000 bits / 10⁶ bps = 8 ms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NAT.
I. NAT lets hosts with private addresses reach the Internet using a public address.
II. NAT converts domain names into IP addresses.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only I is correct. NAT rewrites private source addresses into a public one. Converting domain names to IP addresses is the job of DNS.

questions.q: In TCP Tahoe, a timeout occurs when cwnd is 40 MSS. The new slow-start threshold (ssthresh) becomes
questions.e: On loss, ssthresh is set to half of the current cwnd, that is 20 MSS, and cwnd restarts from 1 MSS.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. In Go-Back-N, the receiver window size is 1.
II. In Selective Repeat, the receiver can buffer frames that arrive out of order.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Go-Back-N discards out-of-order frames, so its receiver window is 1. Selective Repeat has a receiver window larger than 1 and buffers such frames. Both are correct.

questions.q: Which switching technique does NOT need a call set-up phase before data transfer and routes each packet independently?
questions.e: In datagram switching every packet carries the full destination address and is routed on its own. Circuit and virtual-circuit switching first set up a path.

questions.q: A class C network 192.168.1.0 must be divided into at least 6 subnets. Which subnet mask gives the largest number of hosts per subnet?
questions.e: 6 subnets need 3 borrowed bits (2³ = 8 ≥ 6), giving mask /27 = 255.255.255.224 with 2⁵ − 2 = 30 hosts each. Two bits give only 4 subnets.

questions.q: How many valid host addresses are there in the network 10.0.0.0/22?
questions.e: A /22 leaves 10 host bits, so 2¹⁰ = 1024 addresses. Removing the network and broadcast addresses leaves 1022.

questions.q: On a 1 Gbps CSMA/CD network the round-trip propagation time is 20 µs. The minimum frame size needed to detect collisions is
questions.e: The transmission time must be at least the round-trip time. Minimum bits = 10⁹ × 20 × 10⁻⁶ = 20000 bits = 2500 bytes.

questions.q: In a sliding window protocol the frame transmission time is 1 ms and the one-way propagation time is 9.5 ms. The window size needed for 100% link utilisation is
questions.e: Utilisation is 100% when w ≥ 1 + 2a. Here a = 9.5/1 = 9.5, so w = 1 + 19 = 20 frames.

questions.q: A Selective Repeat protocol needs a sender window of 20 frames. The minimum number of bits in the sequence number field is
questions.e: Selective Repeat needs 2ⁿ ≥ 2 × window = 40, so n = 6 (2⁶ = 64). With 5 bits the maximum window would be only 16.

questions.q: Data 1001 is sent using the CRC generator 1011. The transmitted codeword is
questions.e: Append 000 to get 1001000 and divide by 1011 using XOR. The remainder is 110, so the codeword is 1001 followed by 110.

questions.q: A (7,4) Hamming code with even parity places parity bits at positions 1, 2 and 4. The codeword for data bits 1011 (placed at positions 3, 5, 6, 7 in order) is
questions.e: Positions 3,5,6,7 hold 1,0,1,1. p1 covers 3,5,7 = 1,0,1 giving 0. p2 covers 3,6,7 = 1,1,1 giving 1. p4 covers 5,6,7 = 0,1,1 giving 0. Codeword 0110011.

questions.q: A channel has bandwidth 1 MHz and SNR of 30 dB. The Shannon capacity is approximately
questions.e: 30 dB means SNR = 10³ = 1000. C = 10⁶ × log₂1001, and log₂1001 is about 10, so C is about 10 Mbps.

questions.q: A channel has bandwidth 4 kHz and SNR 15. Using Shannon's formula for the limit and Nyquist's formula for the signal levels, the number of levels needed to reach the limit is
questions.e: Shannon: C = 4000 × log₂16 = 16000 bps. Nyquist: 2 × 4000 × log₂L = 16000 gives log₂L = 2, so L = 4.

questions.q: A client sends a SYN with initial sequence number 1000. The server replies with SYN+ACK using initial sequence number 5000. The acknowledgement number in the client's final ACK segment is
questions.e: A SYN consumes one sequence number. The server's SYN+ACK carries seq 5000 and ack 1001. The client acknowledges the server's SYN with ack 5001.

questions.q: An IP datagram of total length 4000 bytes (header 20 bytes) is sent over a link with MTU 1500 bytes. The number of fragments and the fragment offset field value of the last fragment are
questions.e: Data = 3980 bytes. Each fragment carries 1480 data bytes (a multiple of 8), so fragments carry 1480, 1480 and 1020 bytes. The last starts at byte 2960, so offset = 2960/8 = 370.

questions.q: The broadcast address of the subnet containing host 172.16.35.200/20 is
questions.e: A /20 mask has third octet 240, so blocks are 16 wide. 35 lies in block 32 to 47, so the broadcast address is 172.16.47.255.

questions.q: A class B network 172.16.0.0 is subnetted with mask 255.255.255.192. The number of subnets and usable hosts per subnet are
questions.e: Mask /26 on class B borrows 10 bits for subnets: 2¹⁰ = 1024 subnets. Host bits are 6, giving 2⁶ − 2 = 62 hosts.
